slides.title: Variadic Templates Concept
slides.prompt: Variadic templates (introduced in C++11) allow functions and classes to accept an arbitrary number of template arguments using parameter packs (represented by the ellipsis ... token).

slides.title: Parameter Pack Token
slides.prompt: Fill in the three-dot token used to define a template parameter pack.

slides.title: sizeof... Operator
slides.prompt: What is the purpose of the sizeof... operator in C++ variadic templates?
options: It returns the number of elements/arguments contained in a parameter pack at compile time
It calculates the total memory size in bytes of all pack elements combined
It expands the pack into a comma-separated tuple
It checks whether a parameter pack is empty
slides.correctAnswer: It returns the number of elements/arguments contained in a parameter pack at compile time

slides.title: sizeof... Operator Usage
slides.prompt: Fill in the operator name to count arguments in a template parameter pack.

slides.title: Parameter Pack Expansion Placement
slides.prompt: In the call function(args...); where args is a function parameter pack, what does args... do?
options: It expands the pack into a comma-separated sequence of individual arguments
It creates an std::initializer_list containing all elements
It converts the arguments into a std::tuple
It passes arguments as a linked list
slides.correctAnswer: It expands the pack into a comma-separated sequence of individual arguments
